q: Ancient terra-cotta sculptures discovered in Plateau and Kaduna States dating back over 2,000 years belong to the ____ Culture. (P3)
explain: Nok culture produced Africa's earliest terracotta sculptures and iron-smelting evidence.

q: Archaeological excavations of magnificent bronze casting roped pots and burial regalia in Eastern Nigeria revealed the ancient culture of ____. (P3)
explain: Igbo-Ukwu (Anambra State) reveals sophisticated 9th-century bronze metallurgy.

q: The legendary cradle of the Yoruba people where Oduduwa founded the royal dynasty is ____. (P3)
explain: Ile-Ife is revered as the spiritual ancestral home of the Yoruba.

q: The great Northern commercial empire renowned for trans-Saharan trade that flourished for over a thousand years was ____. (P3)
explain: Kanem-Borno controlled key trans-Saharan trade routes across Lake Chad.
